form_en: Ash-coloured crystal with a golden tip
lore_en:
The crystal lay within the eye of a defaced sun statue. Its gold point had grown from mineral receiving first light through one mountain cleft for generations; lamp oil, fire and hot gold could never wake it. When snow sealed the opening, the keeper carried it to the summit to receive the first ray still reaching earth.

He turned its point towards the valley. Dawn opened beneath the clouds, lighting every roof in the storm’s darkness; the lost saw their road home before the sky brightened. As the final ray withdrew into stone, one gold edge turned clear. A prayer upon the plinth said day must be recognised by something upon earth. The keeper merely kept the coat dried in a morning beneath winter.
use_en: Receive first sunlight and aim the gold point towards a hidden region so true dawn unfolds there, dispelling night and granting sunlight not yet due to reach it. Set the crystal upon a threshold so its first ray becomes a road of light, guiding travellers through directionless darkness to the place where it received the sun.

form_en: Slab gem with silver and black faces
lore_en:
The stone was found between blank pages of a book whose spine had burned. A scribe had mixed silver mineral powder into the paper; during the fire its layers pressed around a space awaiting unwritten words. Water placed upon the black face moved at once to the silver, leaving the beginning empty as a message already sent.

Its keeper traced a door in water and pressed the stone to a prison. The real door left the wall and appeared behind the slab, leaving room for a person to pass. He returned it before the water dried, so the lock sounded in its proper place at the next watch. Since then the silver face has borne a black hinge-mark, and every passing drop feels cold from another room.
use_en: Draw an object’s complete shape in water and press the black face to it so it leaves its place and appears beyond the silver face, leaving a real opening. Stroke the wet outline backwards upon silver to return the transferred object to its former position, closing the opening in its original shape.

form_en: Blue mineral nodule inside a brown shell
lore_en:
The nodule opened beneath a mountain, revealing two halves refusing contact within one shell. They had crystallised from ore seams advancing towards each other through generations of shifting earth; the shell grew around their meeting, holding both just before collision. When a miner pressed them, mountain ranges appeared within the gap, small enough for chisel dust to conceal.

As tunnel walls began closing upon his company, he placed the nodule in the cleft and opened its halves. The mountain parted; a sunlit valley appeared between formerly continuous strata, and the miners followed it outside. The nodule returned with another crack in its shell. Within its gap stood the shadow of a new peak, where the miner had set his hand to keep the halves apart.
use_en: Set the nodule between two portions of one mass and open its halves so the shell’s gap becomes a real valley, parting fortress or mountain for travellers. Close the shell around two received marks so their bearers keep their distance despite waves, earth or pressure forcing them together.

form_en: A white miniature tree bearing one amber fruit
lore_en:
The tree rose from the grave of a burnt orchard. It bore one fruit containing its mother's root-system, down to severed roots. Cuttings became ordinary trees; killing the mother killed the seed. Tree ash mingled with amber mineral grains from the orchard’s shattered well; the young roots drank both before the first rains.

Keepers must await one life ending before another begins. Generations have passed beside the same fruit. Tradition says the destroyed orchard has compressed its whole right of return into one seed, learning to outwait human greed.
use_en: When the mother dies naturally, sow its fruit in the former orchard’s soil to restore its lost forest within one dawn, bearing the forms and ages it had before the burning. Let roots touch living trees to gather their forms into the fruit, preserving a forest through fire, flood or generations of desolation.

form_en: White orchid veined with a golden handprint
lore_en:
The bulb came from a gardener's hand in a frozen glasshouse. It opened to its first keeper's touch-pattern; successors learnt it and still waited for petals to relax. The imprint altered slowly as the plant aged. Throughout his life he had mixed a white mineral into its water; as his hand closed, the bulb had grown through a ring bearing the same stone.

A touch can be taught; the first hand has long become earth. Each flowering resembles a recognition between a living thing and the habit of someone dead, sustained by care itself.
use_en: Repeat the first pattern of touch to manifest the gardener’s hands upon every root-linked plant, tending an entire garden overnight with movements the orchid preserved. Set the orchid among sleeping plants so the remembered tending passes through soil, awakening every surviving bud together while winter remains outside.

form_en: Dwarf willow with ring roots enclosing a blue drop
lore_en:
The willow arrived with a sea-drop held among its roots, intact even when inverted. Added salt emerged upon leaves as white coasts. Its sailor-grower recorded one old leaf resembling his island before erosion. The root ring had grown through a blue mineral nodule inside a wreck; when it dissolved, seawater occupied its place among roots turned translucent.

Each flake is kept by date. Perhaps the tree merely transfers salt. Tradition says a sea has learnt to grow on land, trying to remember its shores one leaf at a time.
use_en: Immerse the root ring so its central drop opens as a sea gate, admitting a whole tide into a dry basin and gathering it back when the leaves close. Lay a leaf bearing the right salt trace upon water to raise its remembered island shore beneath one’s feet, sustaining people and ships upon land the sea has swallowed.

form_en: A blue rose with suspended detached petals
lore_en:
The rose stood in a room where every other flower was dust. Severed petals hung in place and travelled with the pot; Vestigium-water stirred them like a hand ceasing to release. Generations of seed yielded flowers that fell normally. Mineral dust from the cracked vase entered the stem on the day the room was abandoned; blue veins closed around the instant the petals began to part.

Keepers chart each interval. They tend the end of a flowering that refused to proceed to decay, every suspended petal reserving a place loss has not yet entered.
use_en: Lay a petal upon a break so separated pieces remain standing in their former shape, sustaining a fallen bridge, collapsing tower or torn hull through an evacuation. Recall placed petals to draw their captive pieces together for one final joining, closing a break whose edges remain complete.

form_en: Blue-black bamboo with a silver shoot-shadow
lore_en:
A bamboo-tip's shadow appeared before its shoot. Its keeper recorded lines that became stems and others that remained upon the wall like unlived trees. Moving the pot broke the correspondence. Its roots touched a mineral mirror buried beneath the wall, where shadows of unsprouted shoots had appeared throughout a rainy season.

Only this plant sustains that waiting. Its grower leaves an entire wall to what it might become. Among these stems, the future has leaves and can perish before it grows.
use_en: Guide the shoot shadows over bare ground to manifest the bamboo forest of future seasons as real stems, bridging a gulf, holding a flood or lifting travellers across a chasm. Cut a shadow before it becomes a stem to erase that particular growth, forcing a root piercing a wall to seek another road in the present.

form_en: Ivory lotus holding one smooth black seed
lore_en:
The pod shows one seed while scales record a tidal weight. The first counter closed his eyes and lost the sequence before one. The seed remains whole; a crack circles it without contact. Its bulb grew around a hollow mineral nodule, nourished by a tide entering and returning through one cleft although the two passages never met.

Its grower calls it a seed reserved before the garden learnt division. Two scales continue disputing its weight while the eye sees one thing waiting to be counted into the world.
use_en: Set the seed upon an object and close the pod, gathering the weight of uncounted seeds into it to pin a warship or sliding mountain. Open the pod beneath an object touched by the seed to withdraw its weight from the world for one breath, allowing a tower to float above collapsing foundations.

form_en: Dwarf tree with ivory leaves and blue scriptlike veins
lore_en:
The sole tree grew from the spine of a book washed blank. Nearby writing shaped its leaf-veins, always with a small error; separated too long, they whitened. Its grower once offered his mother's letter and kept the leaf that omitted his name. Old ink within the spine had joined mineral powder the scribe scattered to dry his pages; the roots found their road into writing through that dust.

Leaves remain beside their models, every reading paired with its silence. The grower's tale calls it a forest learning the language people use to summon one another home.
use_en: Place a written route beneath the roots so leaf veins establish that road between its named places, carrying the leaf’s bearer across the distance in one turning of the page. Nourish a letter with sap so its words manifest as a scene around the reader, preserving the voice and events its author directly witnessed.

form_en: A black lichen disc with a horizontal golden line
lore_en:
The lichen grew on the last rock left above a rising tide. Its gold line remained level when tilted; divided fragments lost it, and spores yielded ordinary growth. Tidal water had washed a gold mineral vein upon the host stone, nourishing the lichen where sky and sea met at the final rising tide.

The salvager brought stone and roots together, calling it a horizon willing to remain on land. Seen level, the line almost disappears. A world may lie beyond it, its prospect sustained by one living web that a careless hand could tear.
use_en: Turn the host stone until its gold line meets the true horizon, drawing a once-seen distant shore beside the observer so ships cross as though through a narrow channel. Touch the gold line to the ground so the visible region accepts its level, keeping buildings upright amid tilting earth or rising waves.

form_en: a wine-coloured octopus with eight gold rings
lore_en:
An octopus nested above an abyss where deep currents swept loose stone away each night. Holding eight stones around its eggs through a red tide, it released them to hunt; they stayed in water, forming a roof without supports. Young learned to choose stones before learning colour changes.

They eat crabs and molluscs and build suspended stone nests that exclude large predators. Divers ask a familiar animal to hold guideposts or shelter wreck fragments during lifting, offering each object to an arm. Moving the animal from its den drops the whole roof, so coastal people protect nests as living reefs.
use_en: Hold eight stone objects in position in water after release.~Roof over the Abyss

form_en: a grey horse with white gold-threaded mane
lore_en:
A horse led snowbound travellers home through a night that overturned every road marker. Returning for the last survivor, its hooves found each former step beneath newly buried ground. A silver road opened through snow with its stride, guiding the living towards the first safe shelter.

Its lineage lives in herds, grazes around imprinted routes and chooses harness companions seasonally. Rescue stations allow a free return after the first journey and record stopping points before entrusting lost travellers. The horse also remembers paths now turned to chasms; guides must read present ground alongside the old road.
use_en: Retain a return route after bringing someone to safety.~Road beneath Snow

form_en: a small grey whale with silver markings
lore_en:
A whale passed a sunken fleet as the last ship’s bell ceased moving. It received that rhythm into its skull; thereafter its calls woke bells in deep water while water around their clappers remained still. Wrecks answered across miles of darkness, making a sounding map of things forgotten by the surface.

It follows deep shoals, rests in chasms with low bells and calls its kind through long ringing intervals. Sailors listen through hulls to locate wreck fields, anchor clear of its passage and leave some bells in each region. Those remaining guide its migration.
use_en: Make submerged bells ring through its song.~Map of Answers

form_en: an old brown hound with amber eyes
lore_en:
Quay hounds lived beside mooring stones veined with salt-soaked white ore. When a rescue boat arrived amid confused people and luggage, one ignored a wet coat and found its wearer beneath the planks. Mineral on its nose had learned to distinguish a living person’s trace from scent left on possessions.

They eat fish exchanged with porters, form packs around quays and recognise passengers through touch. Search teams introduce a traveller before boarding and let the hounds move freely among luggage. Traffickers attempt to break traces with unfamiliar minerals; quay wardens protect the pack’s customary water.
use_en: Distinguish a recent passenger from objects bearing their scent.~Nose of the Last Quay

form_en: a white gull with blue-dappled wings
lore_en:
The gull sought its nest after an island sank during a night of risen seas. It circled the absence until dawn; beneath its wings two horizons folded, making departure quay and lost nest visible along one shining line. Since then it has closed unfinished voyages by letting both ends retain one direction despite changes in the intervening world.

It fishes outside the closure, nests on rocks exposed at deep tide and recognises mates through fog-spanning calls. Captains wait for a complete voluntary flight, then follow its light where compass needles lose direction. Harbours provide perches and food while navies contend for sight of the first opening wing.
use_en: Show both voyage ends along one direction through mist and storm.~Continuous Sea Trace

form_en: a white hart with green buds on its antlers
lore_en:
The hart stood in woodland leafless for years, antlers entering low clouds laden with pollen from the last spring. When the first bud opened, snow retreated into white walls and a hillside germinated in a morning. Spring thereafter moved with its steps, a growing domain able to cross unended winter.

It feeds on shoots within its own domain, leaves enough plants for following animals and sleeps for weeks while its antlers dry. Foresters guard its resting grounds, carry dormant seeds to the route’s edge and yield first grazing to wild creatures. Cities seeking a visit must leave a green corridor through their walls.
use_en: Push winter’s boundary from a hillside along its route.~Call Dormant Seeds

form_en: a pale gold jellyfish with a blue core
lore_en:
The jellyfish arose in a trench where deep currents struck a fissure in time. A shoal of fry hung between contractions as the jellyfish shone in a ring. When its tentacles opened, they continued the interrupted swimming beat while sand beyond the ring had reached the seabed.

It eats plankton, drifts along dark trenches and breeds when temporal currents match the tide. Diving crews mark its light to draw casualties through collapsing stone; contact must precede the held beat. Physicians use it only with observed small aquatic life, for life resumes with all its injuries intact.
use_en: Suspend the ongoing contraction of a creature touching its tentacle ring.~Slowed Water Ring

form_en: a long black-scaled fish with a luminous crest
lore_en:
The dragonfish appeared at an abyssal mouth where a rocky island left the sea’s surface. Its mane burned silver, lighting trees that had vanished from the water above. Those shadows held depth and distance; fish swam through a forest recently lost to the present while remaining in real seawater.

It hunts among shadows of passing shoals, shelters in complete darkness and spawns when deep currents bring new silt. Wreck searchers extinguish other lamps to revisit things recently passing through a water region, tracing lost cargo and final dives. Strong light on its mane collapses the shadow region into the present.
use_en: Reveal a water region and recently departed objects as deep silver shadows.~Last Dive Trace

form_en: an ivory spider with eight gold-jointed legs
lore_en:
The spider wove across a stone gateway split by a landslide season. Threads from one cocoon kept their direction though half the gate moved to another valley; at the web’s centre the spider stepped across lost ground while still touching silk. A homeward path grew from relations between threads rather than distances across land.

It hunts insects reaching the web’s ends and breeds only after a season of quiet at the centre. Guides carry paired ends over passes and keep the centre in a tended station. Matching tension lets them find one another through storms, while the spider closes passage when its nest is threatened.
use_en: Preserve the relation of paired cocoon threads across distance.~Silken Way Home

form_en: a brown bird with an ice-white throat
lore_en:
The nightingale sang on the last leafy tree as winter took the valley. Cold gathered into its nest of refugees’ discarded cloth; at the final note water flowed below. An entire frost wave curled into that fabric as silent music, awaiting the exact melody to return.

It eats insects and dried fruit on trees sustained by the warm region and nests with mineral-bearing cliff fibres. Valley keepers hang cloth beneath the canopy and carry filled winters to remote stone vaults. Lords seeking weapons must preserve the tree, mineral source and the bird’s willingness to sing.
use_en: Draw a cold wave from a valley patch into cloth beneath its song.~Cold-Locking Note

form_en: a silver tortoise with a clouded mirror shell
lore_en:
The tortoise surfaced on a night when mineral cloud hid the moon for a season. A patch of sky caught in its shell, retaining trees and towers reflected on the lake. Years later it crossed a square whose tower was gone and reopened the light, raising the tower’s shadow under the former moon’s bearing.

It grazes aquatic plants, sleeps in deep mud and chooses clear nights to replace its shell-sky. Surveyors place reference objects by the lake before moonrise and compare former shadows with changed foundations. Viewers must stand within the light boundary, where another night still governs the shapes of things.
use_en: Retain moonlight and the object shadows upon it.~Night Raises Shadows

form_en: a brown reindeer with silver-spotted black antlers
lore_en:
The reindeer watched while a storm erased the horizon. Wolf steps from beyond a ridge knocked upon its antlers; night folded around the herd into a ring with one boundary on every side. Whoever crossed that boundary left a step within the antlers, whether approaching by earth, snow or darkness.

It eats lichen, exchanges watches with its mate and keeps calves at the centre. Ice travellers seek sleep near the herd, sheathe weapons on entry and follow the antlers’ warning direction. Armies learn to avoid the boundary rather than conceal footsteps; the ring senses entry itself.
use_en: Set a protective boundary around the sleeping herd.~Antlers Hear Steps

form_en: a solitary gold bee with glass-clear wings
lore_en:
When ice-sea swallowed the final flower meadow, the bee carried pollen across the season’s boundary and returned after a year that had not passed within its body. Its golden abdomen retained the relations between flower, soil and former neighbouring life. Each season one fertilised seed can restore the lost lineage and draw a flowering season from land erased from the present.

It feeds only on nectar bearing that lineage’s mark; before the first seed germinates it sleeps in a wax hollow outside seasonal rhythm. Seed keepers establish isolated gardens and return plants to suitable earth. Kingdoms contend for one seed a year, since a restored meadow may recall the food chain of herds that left the region.
use_en: Keep viable pollen through years without its flower lineage.~One Seed Returns

form_en: a white carp with one red scale
lore_en:
When the city filled its first well, a carp left in the final bucket. Within its gills the well’s taste opened into a depth absent from the basin. It dived through the basin floor and returned with mud from the former source; beneath the city severed waterways began finding one another through its swimming dreams.

It eats algae from the same watershed, chooses rainy nights to revisit the well and lays clear eggs that have never hatched. Water keepers place its basin on unsealed earth and ask it to reconnect thirsty districts. City builders must negotiate with a source still existing at a depth erased by newer maps.
use_en: Maintain the former well’s source in a gill-bound depth.~Dive through the Floor

form_en: a black horse with one ivory hoof
lore_en:
The horse was pulled from a quay as its final slab collapsed. One ivory hoof remained within its unfinished arriving step, holding that uncompleted landing in its body. Wherever it places that hoof, the lost quay can bear a column’s weight for one stride; the sea must leave room for an arrival still unfinished.

It grazes tidal shores, runs with its herd at dawn and refuses reins pulling seaward. Refugees gather close behind and build a real receiving place before asking for passage across the former quay. Fleets that once promised harbours seek it, hoping to make one landing instant an entrance upon an inaccessible coast.
use_en: Recall the lost quay’s load-bearing surface for one stride.~One Step for a Column

form_en: a small black spider with a round white abdomen
lore_en:
The spider hatched within a banner on a burning wall. As fire consumed the middle, it still stepped between thread ends, its white abdomen bearing a whole relation the world had erased. Its final silk can restore continuity to one thing whose middle is gone; along that line distance must accept the ends as still touching.

It hunts in ordinary webs, lays ordinary eggs and retains its white thread until choosing a break. Keepers bring broken bridge cables, a national banner’s weaving and bell ropes before the web, knowing one repair may redirect a region. Its offspring make ordinary silk; the opportunity belongs to this living creature alone.
use_en: Recognise ends formerly belonging to one continuous line.~The Final Thread

form_en: an old silver owl with honey-coloured eyes
lore_en:
The forest keeper called his owl from a tower when snow erased tower and man together. The silver owl answered through the seasons, and wherever its voice touched ground, the watchman’s seat returned. Through its honey eyes night looked from the absent keeper’s position; routes he had watched appeared despite altered forest and walls.

It hunts mice beneath those sightlines, rests on its former perch and accepts new carers through food. Wardens patrol dangerous routes with it, hearing the old call to open sight through snow. They tend a living will that can refuse, while the absent person remains only the bearing of a call.
use_en: Recognise and retain its first keeper’s voice.~Seat of the Absent

name_vi: Hải Cẩu Của Lỗ Băng Cuối
form_en: a white seal with black eye rings
lore_en:
The seal held its nose to the last icehole as the bay froze to its floor. Its black eye rings opened like two chasms, while water beneath its muzzle joined an unfrozen deep sea. Thereafter the breathing hole crossed every overlapping ice layer at that position, preserving a column of sea within white land.

It hunts in that column, sleeps on the ice rim and calls lost seals through bottom echoes. Rescuers build away from the edge and lower lines through the column to seek people beneath the bay. The fixed lifeline redraws polar maps: vessels must reach the door rather than expect the door to follow them.
use_en: Hold an open water column through ice at its imprinted position.~Muzzle Unseals Frost

form_en: a blue moth with one copper wing
lore_en:
The dye works burned with the formula for an unnamed blue. A moth crossed the flames; one wing turned copper and retained the colour beneath. On wet cloth a coloured dot opened like a door: objects within its light regained the ability to show the hue the world had lost.

It drinks sap from trees once grown for the dye, lays on green leaves and needs weeks in shade to refill its wing. Colour keepers grow those trees beside galleries and wait for voluntary landings before restoring a reference. Painters bring works from many countries, since a hue returned to sight may alter the reading of an ancient map.
use_en: Preserve a hue erased from all former samples.~Returning Colour Dot

form_en: a small black tortoise with an ivory shell hollow
lore_en:
The hand receiving the hatchling belonged to a gatekeeper who had sheltered a column fleeing cold. Its shell hollow retained that open-handed gesture, growing into a refuge that hostile wind must circle. When the tortoise steps onto snowfields, a vast handprint appears in the earth, receiving arrivals as that palm once received a small creature.

It eats soft grass, outlives generations and chooses palms on which to rest. Displaced columns follow its slow pace, camp inside the print and leave central grass for it. Rulers request its mark upon borders; the tortoise opens its shell only when newcomers are truly received into shelter.
use_en: Retain the first palm’s warmth and gesture within the shell hollow.~Earth Opens Its Palm

form_en: Red crystalline powder in a small glass vial
lore_en: Marco opens a vial of red powder while discussing artillery improvements. Warm light falls on his fingers as he explicitly identifies it as Common rank. Mixed into a clinging incendiary compound, it serves Bala de Fuego ammunition. The manuscript does not establish its mineral source or refining process, and this entry leaves both open.
use_en: Supplies heat in an incendiary compound; heat-producing powder also appears with whale fat to reduce ice on sails and rigging.

form_en: Ancient oak timber with densely interwoven grain
lore_en: HMS Red Baron is built from ancient Sherwood oaks whose forest absorbed Vestigium and changed. Unusually tough, interwoven grain lets the hull withstand repeated cannon hits. This entry displays harvested timber as material. The source establishes neither conscious trees nor a hull capable of repairing itself.
use_en: Builds a hull with greater resistance to gunfire than ordinary timber, as demonstrated aboard HMS Red Baron.

form_en: White powder with grey grains
lore_en: The powder was ground from white stone in a mountain hollow where night mist gathered into grey grains before touching the ground. Over many seasons, the stone learned to receive water from the air; its crushed fragments still carried the sleep of mist into storerooms.
use_en: A packet keeps a tool chest or seed bag dry through one damp night.

form_en: Yellow wax stick with silver specks
lore_en: In a toy foundry, a craftsman kept a wax bird's wing beside a snow-filled window. When silver dust fell from the furnace roof, the wing stood upright until morning; that batch of wax retained the persistence of a small thing waiting to take shape.
use_en: The wax allows wings, rims and small mould teeth to be shaped upright by hand before casting.

form_en: Cream sand mixed with blue grains
lore_en: A sandbank beneath a stone bridge once darkened along the steps of an underground stream, warning riverside folk of floods. After the river changed course, its blue grains still answered fresh water; people carried the old warning home to their thresholds.
use_en: A line of sand reveals water creeping through a threshold, barrel stave or storehouse roof.

form_en: Grey paste in an earthen jar
lore_en: A box maker mixed paste with meltwater from an ice block that held an old scrap of paper fast. When his boxes crossed the pass, their wrappings tore but their labels stayed; the paste had taken on the grip of ice that had kept a message through many seasons.
use_en: The paste secures paper labels to medicine jars and cargo chests on cold journeys.

form_en: Pale oil with a blue sheen
lore_en: The oil was pressed from seeds growing around an abandoned mill, their roots winding once around its axle. When the last mill wheel was removed, the oil in the seeds still redrew that turn in blue before falling still.
use_en: A craftsman places a drop on a gear to see where its motion stops or wanders.

form_en: Fine brown powder streaked silver
lore_en: The brown powder lay beneath a cave pool so still that quarrymen could see their hair in it. One night its silver veins parted before the vault fell; thereafter, grains taken from the bottom still gathered at the surface and opened along passing vibrations.
use_en: A dusted water tray helps tunnel workers notice faint vibration through the floor or props.

form_en: Grey lime with coarse white grains
lore_en: The lime was burned from the stonework of a bakery oven that kept embers overnight for the whole street. When the oven was dismantled, white grains in its stones still glowed before smouldering ash, like lit windows after the street had gone to sleep.
use_en: Dusting apparently cold ash marks places an oven cleaner should leave until fully spent.

form_en: Grey flax fibre with a silver sheen
lore_en: The flax was steeped in a stone basin where an old tailor washed unfinished garment samples. Over the years, silver veins in the basin entered the fibre, preserving its first fold like a lesson just passed on.
use_en: Tailors run the fibre along a pattern edge to keep its fold during fitting or wrapping.

form_en: Pale red powder with white flakes
lore_en: The powder was scraped from anchors buried in salt earth after the harbour receded. White scales grew along their corroding iron and kept seeking rust even when ground down; the salvagers brought home something that could point to concealed weakness.
use_en: The powder clings to rust paths in nails, locks and joints, showing craftsmen where to dismantle and inspect.

form_en: Clear resin dotted blue
lore_en: The resin came from trees beside a frozen waterfall, the inner bark always facing its wet spray. When the wind turned, the blue specks clouded before droplets appeared; resin carried from the forest kept that mist-facing direction.
use_en: A piece beneath wrapping warns that mist has reached blankets, dry stores or bandages.

form_en: Black ink with a copper sheen
lore_en: A cargo clerk ground ink with water dripping from a bronze fish throughout the mist season. His first strokes always dried inside a ring of water; bronze dust entering the ink had kept the way a fish's scales divide the current around its body.
use_en: The ink keeps names and tally marks clear on labels exposed to drizzle or melting snow.

form_en: Yellow liquid in a blue vial
lore_en: The fluid was collected from a cliff once beneath the sea. Each thaw, the stone drew white rings around pockets where old brine had rested; a barrel maker caught that habit in a bottle and brought the sea's memory into his workshop.
use_en: The fluid reveals salt left inside food barrels before a fresh filling.

form_en: Red wax containing black grains
lore_en: In a weighhouse, sealing wax was melted for generations over the lamp beside the receipt book. One winter, impressions in a fresh batch darkened when their lids were raised; repeated handovers had left the wax a memory of its first opening.
use_en: A wax bridge across the lid lets a recipient see whether a box has been opened in transit.

form_en: Silver powder blended with grey charcoal
lore_en: The silver powder was found in the bearing of a bell pulley, rubbed by its rope through thousands of mornings. Soot from the watch lamp mixed with the filings; ground together, they held the screech among their grains and let the bell carry farther.
use_en: The powder makes a small pulley quiet enough for its operator to hear instructions from below.

form_en: White thread with minute mineral knots
lore_en: The fibre was spun from white roots beneath a cave roof where water dripped through beads of stone. Through many dry seasons, the roots learned to hold late-arriving water; spun apart, each knot still caught a drop as though saving a place for the next.
use_en: A preparer transfers and counts drops of clear water along a thread into a narrow-necked jar.

form_en: Two-layered blue liquid
lore_en: Green fluid seeped from a bridge step where wagons often halted to let one another pass. Generations of loading and release taught the stone its rhythm, until the water in its cracks reddened under pressure and faded slowly after the weight moved on.
use_en: A fluid layer between two clear faces reveals uneven pressure beneath a mould or band.

form_en: Amber resin containing white grains
lore_en: The resin flowed from a tree in a cold charcoal field, whitening the old burns in its bark each year. When the tree fell, that white layer still slowed flames before they entered the resin; the time the tree had spent closing its wounds had settled into Vestigium.
use_en: A resin coat on a case gives its carrier time to put it down when fire catches.

form_en: Blue ink containing gem dust
lore_en: The ink was ground with blue stone from a stream running through an abandoned mine. The stone's pearly light always gathered in the narrowest water channels; in ink, it kept seeking fine scratches as though returning to its old streambed.
use_en: Craftsmen use the ink to find hairline flaws in knives, needles and engraving tools before handing them over.

form_en: Grey paper pressed with black grains
lore_en: The paper was pressed with water from the floor of an old spice store, where black grains lay beneath each jar. The empty floor still held the scent of past trading seasons; grains worked into paper carried the power to keep one breath of fragrance apart.
use_en: A dry sheet keeps a spice shipment's scent for the buyer to compare on arrival.

form_en: White powder with green grains
lore_en: The white powder was gathered from a kiln floor where steam had crept through cracked bowls for many cold seasons. Green grains grew along those fissures; ground free of the floor, they still sought the old paths when they met glaze and moisture.
use_en: The powder shows a restorer where to brace a fragile ceramic before lifting it from its stand.

form_en: Grey-silver ingot with blue ends
lore_en: The ingot was cast from silver reclaimed from a glasshouse, whose frame had held the night stove against morning ice. Between heat and cold, the metal took on a gentler rhythm of passage; the founder kept its blue ends intact to give that rhythm a road.
use_en: Set between a stove and water tank, the ingot supplies steady warmth to a nursery or glassworking bench.

form_en: Clear liquid carrying golden flakes
lore_en: The fluid was collected from a painter's roof, where generations of sunlight passed through amber glass onto colour studies. Tiny scales in the water kept the hue of the last painting after it was removed; spread over fresh ink, they preserved that same unfading morning.
use_en: The fluid keeps signs, coloured maps and weaving patterns clear through the mist season.

form_en: Purple powder with flat silver grains
lore_en: The purple powder was scraped from stone pillars beneath a theatre floor. Thousands of dancing steps ended there while song remained whole beneath the dome; the silver grains had learned to take vibration inward before it reached the listener.
use_en: Powder beneath a stand steadies sighting glasses, engraving benches and medicine scales against passing footsteps.

form_en: Grey fibre with a red ridge
lore_en: The fibre was drawn from bark curved around a cradle left in a garden. Season after season, branches swayed and returned to shelter it, until red veins in the bark retained that curve; firing the fibre into a new shape gave it another home to return to.
use_en: Woven into a light vent flap or fabric stay, the fibre returns it to its open shape when released.

form_en: Green wax threaded white
lore_en: The wax came from a hive within a well wall, where white threads always grew towards seeping water. When a well keeper pressed the old comb into a crack, the wax gathered at the drip; through many seasons of rising and falling water, the hive had learned to close a fissure's mouth.
use_en: Wax along a barrel or small tank joint builds itself over newly appearing leaks.

form_en: Amber oil containing white bubbles
lore_en: The oil was caught beneath the roof of an abandoned bathhouse, where generations of vapour gathered as white bubbles under amber film. When its final copper gutter was removed, the bubbles burst together as though answering a command; the oil had kept the house's opening rhythm within it.
use_en: The oil times vapour for drying rooms, cloth steamers or small machine vanes through touches of a copper lever.

form_en: Silver ingot with an off-centre black core
lore_en:
The bell sank with a convoy at the sea gate and rang beneath the water until its final note vanished from the shore. Generations later, salvagers found silver within it, with none of its surrounding bronze. The newly cast ingot held an off-centre black heart that always turned towards the place the missing had hoped to reach.

The ingot can receive a call and hold it outside time. Set in the destination harbour’s water, it sounds at once through every metal object that crossed the sea with its speaker, whether lying in an abyss or in distant cities. Listeners know the harbour’s direction through a note heard by them alone.
use_en: Holds a call outside time, then sounds through every metal object that crossed the sea with its speaker.

form_en: Silver liquid in a black vessel
lore_en:
Well diggers in a besieged city reached stone mirror that refused sunlight. Each lowered bucket returned with silver water while the puller’s reflection lingered below. After the city emptied, reflections that had never returned gathered into silver-black fluid, holding a starry sky unseen by anyone above.

Its level surface opens upon a depth beyond the earth. An entire tower or ship can descend if its complete shadow is guided across the silver; within, objects remain whole among motionless constellations. A keeper retaining the tether can haul them back, hearing bells from vanished wells along the returning line.
use_en: Stores inanimate objects in a depth beyond the world by passing their entire shadows across the fluid.

form_en: White fibre with dark joints
lore_en:
When a suspension bridge between two towers collapsed, its keeper’s coat caught the broken chains. Those across the gulf saw him fall, yet its hem held the road whole until the last child crossed. At dawn the coat lay between empty towers, each white thread bearing a dark joint like blood unwilling to leave the body.

Threads drawn from it can be stitched into any continuous thing approaching rupture. When disaster comes, broken parts still share their former load: a bridge hangs over emptiness, a dam holds water with an open crack. Each survivor’s passing step consumes a dark joint until the final thread returns the breaking to the world.
use_en: Defers a structure’s complete rupture, allowing broken parts to bear their shared load during evacuation.

form_en: Black glaze marked by silver
lore_en:
The glaze was fired with timber from a library that burned for seven nights. Opening the kiln, the potter saw lit reading desks beneath its black surface, as though the house had passed through fire into a vessel’s skin. When book ash touched the glaze, pages sounded from a place where the vessel had never held space.

Ash from a burnt object spread upon the glaze in darkness opens its image into a depth one can see and enter. A pinch of house ash restores rooms and furnishings at the instant before ignition; book ash opens readable pages. Visitors walk within the last version of what was lost, carrying it out through memory alone.
use_en: Opens an ash-image space recreating an object or building just before it burned, allowing entry for reading and observation.

form_en: Silver dust with copper-red grains
lore_en:
A death-warrant copyist spent his life scraping names from orders delivered to a citadel. Each reprieve gathered silver dust beneath his nib; on the night the citadel fell, it spilled across the window and every incoming order stopped in midair. The dust was recovered after the papers became birds’ nests.

The powder severs the execution of a written statement. Scattered across a covenant’s opening character, it stills every seal, transmitted command and mechanism deriving instruction from that text throughout its bound domain. The paper remains and people remember, yet between command and consequence opens a blank the world cannot cross.
use_en: Suspends an entire written system’s supernatural execution by interrupting its original command.

form_en: Blue resin enclosing a suspended white layer
lore_en:
A pine across a mountain cleft had lived long enough for its roots to join both cliffs. When the earth parted, its trunk split while the crown still moved as one, because white resin held the instant before the crack. Through winter, resin flowed from both halves into the gulf and hardened as blue drops enclosing a suspended white layer.

Applied to a cut, the resin preserves integrity across distance. A ship’s halves may drift on opposite sides of a strait without admitting water; a tower opens for a procession and closes as though no doorway existed. Force and movement still pass between the halves while the resin’s white line remains intact.
use_en: Keeps separated parts functioning as one intact object, opening passage through a structure without severing its continuity.

form_en: Purple liquid with a floating white edge
lore_en:
The lighthouse’s upper window shattered when waves crossed its rail. In lightning, the sea appeared overhead as well as below the keeper; one glass corner retained two horizons exchanging places. Violet fluid seeping from its reverse bears a floating white rim that gathers towards whatever the holder calls down, even in an inverted hand.

Spread along a straight edge, the fluid changes the fall of inanimate things crossing it. River water can climb a fortress wall and pour along a stone ceiling; cargo rolling from a quay falls sideways into a storehouse. Gravity returns beyond the white rim, as though the object had crossed another world’s horizon.
use_en: Changes gravity’s direction for inanimate things crossing a coated edge, making water and cargo fall along new orientations.

form_en: Thin blue-silver mineral laminate
lore_en:
The mineral lined a tower keeper’s chamber, whose curtains stayed shut after the family departed. Sunlight fell upon its door for generations, laying blue-silver strata like a section through time. When a stranger opened the curtains, the family’s final-day shadows remained upon it, walking towards a road the city had built over.

Each layer holds a real interval of daylight, including the space its light touched. Erected in darkness and pressed open, a layer admits a traveller into that day’s scene, along the old road to its former destination. Those outside see a shadow thin as sunlight through stone; within, the lost afternoon’s wind still blows.
use_en: Opens a route within stored daylight space, joining the panel’s entrance to the light’s former destination.

form_en: Half silver ingot, half arrested droplet
lore_en:
A foundry upon a sunken island emerged when the sea withdrew from the depths. Its furnace held half a silver ingot and a falling drop, suspended between its founder’s first casting and the final casting of their descendants. Every surrounding mould had shattered, yet their shadows circled the drop like fish seeking an unborn shore.

Whoever guides the drop can cast the emptiness between metal masses into one continuous body, joining a fleet into a bridge or separate towers into a single rampart. The joining part bears both shores’ properties though no material stood between them. Its keeper must envision the entire destination form; wherever the drop passes, a portion of the world becomes complete.
use_en: Casts the emptiness between metal masses into continuous material, joining structures on the scale of cities and fleets.

form_en: Black ink drop with a golden rim
lore_en:
The ink stood upon a chronicler’s desk after death prevented the final sentence. Dynasties within the book disappeared, yet its blank page stayed warm as though a hand had just lifted. When the library fell, words from every copy flowed into the bottle, leaving a gold-rimmed black drop bearing the ending history had refused.

The ink writes an unfinished condition upon reality itself: a city remains standing until its last person leaves the gate; a ship retains a homeward road until its watcher extinguishes the lamp. The keeper must write and understand every word by hand. Once the sentence closes, the world holds its waiting portion beyond destruction until the condition is fulfilled.
use_en: Binds an existence under destruction to a completion condition, preserving it until that condition occurs.

form_en: Blue loop without a visible splice
lore_en:
The shroud was woven for a sailor who never returned. The watcher at home added a length whenever the waves delivered old wreckage, until its first edge met its last although the cloth still filled the room. At the weaver’s burial, it drew into a loop of green thread, and the room’s door opened upon distant surf.

The loop can be stretched into two closed boundaries at places it has touched. Within them, distance loses its intervening portion: someone crossing a city gate emerges upon a ship beyond the horizon, and an entire river may continue through a vast loop. The two places become opposite sides of one stitch.
use_en: Joins two closed boundaries into one continuous passage, carrying people, ships and flowing water across great distance.

form_en: White glaze holding three blue drops
lore_en:
A highland potter collected rain in one vessel through three drought seasons. In the fourth, he followed the clouds and never returned; the vessel broke upon its plinth, leaving three blue drops upon white glaze. Each held a moving cloud whose shadow followed a wind the outer sky had forgotten.

Turning a drop skyward summons an entire stored rainy season, placing an earlier year’s sky above the land beneath the shard. Rivers regain lost watercourses, and buried seeds hear the rainfall that woke their ancestors. The keeper chooses the season, while its summoned sky brings its own wind, thunder and duration.
use_en: Replaces a region’s sky with one of three stored rainy seasons, restoring its winds and water cycle.

form_en: Black wax block with a white seal
lore_en:
A granary seal melted on the night the city walls broke, yet its white impression remained upon black wax. The keeper had promised the door would open only after every family received its portion; at dawn the besiegers found the surrounding wall fallen while grain was still being distributed within. The wax lay beneath the last person’s departing feet.

The block seals a physical boundary through its setter’s promise. Within it, destruction stops at the outer face: a sea hangs over a broken dam, city stones stand around excavated foundations. People within live and work until the promised task is fulfilled, while every load waits beyond one white seal.
use_en: Seals a structural region beyond collapse until its setter’s specific promise is fulfilled.

form_en: Silver foil crossed by a red line
lore_en:
The mirror in an old station faced the wall from the day its final carriage departed. Generations of watchers touched its silver back as though reaching someone beyond it. When the station was dismantled, the silver peeled into a thin red-lined leaf, while the bricks behind it showed an intact platform beneath an unfamiliar sky.

Dividing the leaf makes two surfaces one face. Keepers may press a map, armour plate or wall section here against its counterpart there, exchanging the entire touching faces across distance. A burning rampart’s face can become distant quarry stone; new red lines record each occasion on which the world changed its skin.
use_en: Exchanges two surfaces touching the leaf’s halves, transferring the entire outer layer of objects or structures across distance.

form_en: Grey dust with one remaining golden grain
lore_en:
During a night without horizons, refugees followed gold dust falling from the gap between two constellations. Each step extinguished a grain and opened another stretch through waters marked dead upon every map. When the last refugee reached a bright shore, grey dust gathered in the guide’s bottle, leaving one gold grain belonging to a star that had never been born.

That final grain summons a road outside the world, joining two flames it has recognised during darkness. Travellers see the entire sky beneath their feet and cities as distant embers. Outer distance contracts with the breaths the guide still holds; a company may cross seas or continents that offer no remaining passage.
use_en: Opens an otherworldly night road between two marked flames, carrying a company beyond distance and impassable lands.

form_en: One silver drop in a blue tube
lore_en:
Rock rose from an ice sea on the morning sunlight first touched a ravine dark for generations. A pathfinder saw the light’s boundary stand like a blade between the cliffs; at its foot, a silver drop held a retreating mountain shadow. Captured in a green tube, it arrested the ravine’s dawn until the finder left the shore.

The fluid opens a boundary between true day and sky severed from the sun. Guiding the drop along a horizon, its keeper can bring a night-bound region into daylight, placing the sun where the world’s shape had concealed it. Ice, plants and people receive real light and heat; the giving daylight region loses precisely the sky transferred.
use_en: Transfers true day’s boundary between two skies, bringing the sun and its heat to land hidden by the world’s shadow.

form_en: Black coal with faint golden grain
lore_en:
A coal seam emerged beneath a bathhouse long buried in snow. The last hot water drained into cracks on the night its roof fell; when the site was dug out, the coal’s golden grain remained as warm as a bench someone had just left. A stoker kept a lump beside the broken basin to remember its discovery.

The coal receives furnace heat and releases it slowly through its surface, enough to warm a small sleeping room through a night watch. As it cools, the gold retreats into the core; household keepers set spent lumps aside to return to the hearth next day.
use_en: Keeps sleeping rooms, casualty carts and medicine stores warm.

form_en: Round blue pebbles in a copper cage
lore_en:
At the foot of a mill swept away by flood, pebbles rolled back up the bank whenever the water ebbed. They had lain between two millstones throughout a hungry season, while villagers took turns pushing the wheel by hand because the river had frozen. The millwright gathered them into a copper cage and heard turning timber within the smooth stones.

Immersed in flowing water, the whole cage tilts steadily in one direction and draws a small shaft attached to it. Millers use that force for grain-drying fans, leaving the great wheel’s strength for newly arrived sacks.
use_en: Drives drying fans, stirrers and small pumps in riverside workshops.

form_en: Porous brown earth with soft white threads
lore_en:
A nursery beside a windthrown grove held pockets of earth that curled around bare roots. Through the previous winter, its keeper had wrapped each seedling in old clothing and buried them beneath larger trees. As the cloth decayed, white threads appeared in the soil, retaining the shape of the hands that had banked each stem.

The earth forms a light ball that holds air around roots during jolting cart journeys. At the new bed, growers water it and open its edges; the threads gradually release in warm soil, allowing the roots to find their own way onward.
use_en: Transports seedlings and shelters roots exposed by landslips.

form_en: Amber salt grains in a linen pouch
lore_en:
In a half-burnt granary, seeds beneath a salt jar sprouted while snow still covered the door. Firefighting water had carried salt through straw ash and frozen upon the jar’s mouth, where the keeper had rested a hand while counting the remaining sowing portions. The new amber crystals crackled faintly in light.

A salt pouch beside a sowing tray wakes living seeds within the same morning, letting gardeners tend one cohort together. After awakening them, the salt pales; old pouches hang apart from fresh seed to preserve the sowing schedule.
use_en: Coordinates greenhouse sowing and helps make use of short growing seasons.

form_en: Ivory linen with closed red stitchwork
lore_en:
At an aid station abandoned after a rockfall, the last bandage roll remained dry among basins of red water. Its washer had joined many scraps with one thread and kept washing until the well froze into a mirror. When sunlight returned, the red stitching had closed into small rings, each enclosing clean cloth.

The cloth draws blood from the dressing’s inner face to its outer layer, letting attendants see saturation without repeatedly uncovering a wound. Separate lengths are stored in medicine chests; a used piece carries its red mark for life.
use_en: Makes dressing saturation visible during rescue and wound care.

form_en: White ceramic with blue grain beneath its glaze
lore_en:
A potter set aside the batch fired on a night when snow blocked the kiln door. Families waited outside for medicine jars; within, the fire consumed the last shelf boards. On opening the kiln, the potter found blue grain beneath the glaze like veins in a cold hand. The jars cooled to human warmth and held it throughout the night.

Sherds from that firing line medicine boxes to soften temperature changes on the road. Keepers place one sherd outside the box; when its blue grain whitens, the entire lining must return to a warm room.
use_en: Shelters cold-sensitive medicines during relief journeys.

form_en: Brown resin threaded with flax-like light
lore_en:
After a flood, a boatyard exhausted its stitching cord and held joints with resin from a willow trunk lodged between two hull frames. Through the repair season, the living wood rooted in wet shavings. When workers lifted the trunk away, its resin drew into shining threads, joining plank faces along the grain as though it had learned the roots’ paths.

The resin holds a dry split while workers fit a lasting brace. Its threads change colour with the timber bearing strain, leaving a record of heavy seas for the next repair.
use_en: Mends furniture, stretchers and hull planks pending reinforcement.

form_en: Coarse silver sand in a wooden box
lore_en:
A bell founder kept the sand beneath a cracked bell because each night it trembled with the missing portion of its voice. For years it had lain in the plinth’s hollow, bearing the strokes that called workers home from dark fields. When the workshop floor was raised, silver grains ringed a cavity below, though a sweeper had just levelled them.

Scattered around a cold mould, the sand shifts towards thin walls or enclosed cavities. Founders follow the silver rings to choose areas for closer inspection, using one box through many seasons until its trembling falls silent.
use_en: Helps inspect casting moulds, bells and machine parts before use.

form_en: Grey slabs with concentric white rings
lore_en:
After an earthquake, a storehouse floor held slabs that had slid apart beneath columns still standing straight. They came from a cliff struck repeatedly by avalanches, each season adding a white ring around the grey core. Builders had used them as level thresholds; only when the walls shook did the white rings open like eyelids beneath a heavy dream.

A slab yields a short distance to spread a jolt travelling through a column’s foot. Afterwards its opened rings retain their gaps, showing builders which foundation sections need replacement before the storehouse returns to service.
use_en: Beds storehouses, machinery and columns in places subject to shaking.

form_en: Black fibres with silver points at both ends
lore_en:
In a grinder’s chest abandoned on a mountain pass, sheath-lining fibres still held the shapes of blades removed from them. They came from bark grown around an old whetstone where travellers had sharpened knives before winter. Each black strand bore a silver point at either end, as though preserving the instant an edge paused between two strokes.

Woven into a lining, the fibres keep an edge away from its sheath’s walls when the bearer runs or falls. Armourers store surgical knives as well as swords in it; old sheaths are opened for inspection when the silver points dim.
use_en: Lines weapon sheaths and sharp-tool cases for transport.

form_en: Brown-black glaze on thin ceramic tiles
lore_en:
A glazier built her kiln beside a forge whose hammers followed her child into sleep each afternoon. She placed flawed tiles beneath the anvil to soften the floor’s trembling. After a season sharing both furnaces’ heat and cold, the dark glaze began retaining the first impact’s sound and releasing it as a murmur after nightfall.

The glazed tiles soften knocking carried from a small workshop into adjoining rooms. After work, craftspeople take them into the yard and hear the stored sound return; their surfaces brighten when the final murmur fades into the wind.
use_en: Beds anvils and workbenches and lines partitions around craft workshops.

form_en: Thin copper leaves with wave-like grain
lore_en:
At the foot of a burnt clock tower, workers recovered copper leaves fallen from its pendulum. Fire had consumed the dial while the keeper still counted hours for fugitives crossing the bridge; each call rang into the stairwell and vanished in smoke. The leaves cooled with evenly closed waves, still trembling to the beat of the pendulum melted across the floor.

Beside a turning shaft, a copper leaf trembles out of step when the shaft misses a familiar beat. Machine keepers hang it within sight to notice a slipping belt or catching gear before the whole workshop stops.
use_en: Monitors mills, pumps and cargo hoists.

form_en: Bone compass with a gold lid
lore_en:
A sailor without a homeland was given a place beside a stranger’s hearth. He repaired a broken compass with bone from their final meal and returned to sea; the needle kept pointing towards that kitchen despite his attempts to name his birthplace. On a stormy night its golden lid opened and a warm streak crossed the water, leading him to the very door.

The compass has since taken the place where its bearer was most sincerely welcomed as their private north. While someone there willingly keeps the door open, the needle can draw the homeward road closer; between waves or mountain ranges, a familiar stretch appears with the smoke-scent of the waiting house.
use_en: Guides the lost towards true welcome and opens a stretch home while someone still waits.

form_en: Ebony music box with a silver spindle
lore_en:
The box-maker built it for a singer weakened by illness. She sang her final song beside its silver spindle, preserving even the long pauses for breath. After the funeral the family wound it; the room within the song opened around them, with every person’s chair and an empty place where the singer had sat.

The box opens fully only when someone will listen to the end. During the music, keepsakes once touched by the singer recover familiar movements: a curtain stirs, a book turns to a passage once read. The room may dwell again in the way one person made it home until the final note returns every object to silence.
use_en: Holds remembrance within a remembered room and lets the living freely release part of their mourning.

form_en: Gold seal shaped as a folded bird
lore_en:
A courier buried to the shoulders by an avalanche still remembered a bird-mark on an envelope. He crawled after the feeling of an unfinished duty until a slit of light led back to the old road. On delivery the golden seal folded its wings, taking his memory of the storm that had nearly held him.

The seal has since accepted one letter and one willing courier. Each wrong turn stirs the bird within their mind. When the real road is severed, the courier may surrender a familiar route-memory for the bird to open one crossing; on the far side the recipient’s name sounds like wings touching a door.
use_en: Preserves the duty of delivering one letter and crosses a broken route through the courier’s memory.

form_en: Black lens in a silver frame
lore_en:
The lenses were ground from an eraser of records’ mirror. When he first wore them, deleted lines stood around the room in black script, each joined to his hand by a silver thread. Touching one, he reread words he had been paid to bury.

The glasses receive erasures as doorways still joined to their erasers’ minds. Readers see words on their former material and follow silver threads into earlier pages, travelling backwards through concealment. Every recovered line leaves part of the reader’s own past within its blank space.
use_en: Recovers scraped records and the traces of successive concealment.

form_en: Round mirror edged with lead
lore_en:
The craftsman turned the mirror towards an empty chair and signed his willing departure while it recorded. Returning, he found the reflected seat indented beneath an unseen person’s weight. The unfinished signature on the lead rim lengthened by one stroke, and the room’s image opened deep through the glass.

The mirror preserves the world’s portion that appears only when its authorised witness freely leaves. The absent witness chooses someone else to look in their stead. That person may enter the image and walk among objects present during the unwitnessed interval, but every step requires the absent witness to acknowledge it with a stroke of their name.
use_en: Investigates a deliberate absence through an observer chosen by its witness.

form_en: White stone inkwell
lore_en:
The inkwell stood between two people who had lost their homes in a land dispute. Together they drew a boundary and signed beneath it. The following night a dark line appeared on the real land, crossing snow, new walls and displaced markers. Their descendants changed the story, yet the boundary still rose beneath their names whenever the map opened.

The ink preserves what both sides freely accepted as a bordered line. An oath written in it may become a threshold across clearly named land; crossing leaves behind every privilege its bearer freely promised to surrender. To change the boundary, those still entitled to acknowledge it must stand together upon its former course.
use_en: Preserves a mutually acknowledged boundary and makes signatories’ crossings of their pledge manifest.

form_en: Small harp with crystalline strings
lore_en:
The musician built the harp fearing death before morning. He drew its crystal strings towards the window and played until the sun cleared the roofs; that dawn’s light remained between them. After his death, his daughter plucked the first note in a shuttered room and saw the horizon open where a wall stood.

The harp preserves one complete dawn, from its first light to the last early birdsong. A player may spread it around a room or weave it into a shining route through darkness. During that interval, each listener may see something once promised for a new day appear as a standing shadow before them.
use_en: Opens a dawn for a company in darkness and helps them acknowledge work they still wish to undertake.

form_en: Charred wooden frame sheathed in gold
lore_en:
The frame was recovered from a burnt house and passed among those who had occupied a room before the flames arrived. Each saw only black timber. For the final survivor it opened the entire room as their eyes retained it, including blur where they had closed their eyes.

The last witness signs beneath the frame to let a later person enter the scene. Each added stroke opens another doorway within; passing every door receives all that one life can still bear. When the name is complete, the frame chooses a willing recipient who remained until the end, giving the scene a living place beyond its witness’s death.
use_en: Hands an entire testimony on the verge of extinction to one willing living recipient.

form_en: Crown; exact construction remains undescribed
lore_en: Isabella identifies the Crown of Ravenna as a Mythic Vestigium held at the centre of Western Roman power, connecting it with campaign anomalies beyond ordinary military and logistical explanation. She also admits that its full powers remain unknown, and later reminds Testarossa that she has never seen it herself. This record preserves the distinction between intelligence assessment and direct observation.
use_en: Assessed as strategically important enough to justify recovery or destruction; its precise operating mechanism remains unconfirmed.

form_en: Heirloom bell; material not described
lore_en: An archival case describes a bell that rings when two people sworn to return to one home enter the same city. Over more than forty years in a seafaring family, it rises from Common through Rare to Wondrous. Repeated reunions after storms reinforce its relational rule; advancement stops when its final keeper stores it away and ends the pattern of use.
use_en: Signals that two people bound by the shared oath are within one city, helping them reunite after a voyage.

name_vi: Ống kính Ngọn Hải Đăng Cuối
form_en: Brass spyglass holding a motionless flame
lore_en:
The lighthouse keeper looked through the spyglass one last time before his tower fell. He saw a ship still seeking its coastal bearing and held his gaze upon it until water crossed the doorway. Months later sailors recovered the glass with a flame standing within; aimed at the former foundations, it opened the final night and the ship not yet in harbour.

Oil poured into the brass rim feeds only a tiny flame, yet an observer may entrust a watch to draw the lighthouse beam onto the sea. Within that light, the final night’s water-route rises among present waves like another passage still awaiting completion. The guide sees both seas together and must choose which portions remain real enough for a ship to sail.
use_en: Preserves the lost lighthouse’s bearing and opens a guiding beam for one ship along its former coast.

form_en: White bow with a divided black string
lore_en:
During the last siege of a nameless valley, an archer stood before a ravine whose cries took many heartbeats to cross. The archer drew the black string’s branches apart, then joined them. A fathom of night folded between the cliffs; an arrow bearing a rescue line appeared across the gulf before the bowstring’s sound had left the archer’s ears.

Ever since, the bow has carried a crease in distance. Its wielder can place the crease’s shores along any visible course of flight. Rain, fire and arrows within the folded stretch continue falling through their own world, while the arrow passes through the dark seam like thread through a needle. The string’s branches join only when both ends truly offer room for passage.
use_en: Folds a fathom of flight, carrying an arrow beyond fire, wind or a storm of arrows within that stretch.

form_en: White gauntlet crossed by one black crack
lore_en:
When a cliffside temple’s vault collapsed, its gatekeeper raised a white hand between the leaning columns. The stone mass stopped above the fleeing congregation. Dust still fell and bells tore loose, while the glove’s black crack crept from wrist to fingertip like the shadow of an ending held in one palm.

The glove can arrest one falling object, even a mass as large as a fortress roof. While held, every connected fragment stands still together; those beneath may cross a hall about to become a tomb. When the hand lowers, its weight returns entire. Heirs to the glove often tie a rope around their wrist so the last survivor knows when to pull them from their station.
use_en: Arrests a collapsing mass, granting time for evacuation or supports.

form_en: Enclosed helm with a golden mouth slit
lore_en:
On the night the sea entered a harbour city, its last commander removed his helmet, called each company’s name into the steel and gave it to a boatman. He remained upon steps flooded to his knees. The boatman donned it at the outer harbour, and the old voice rose from his mouth, crossing the surf to soldiers upon the seawall.

Ever since, the helmet has held a freely given voice. Its bearer can carry that voice across a battlefield so everyone once called by name hears it as though the former speaker stood beside them. The breath belongs to the living; each word brightens the golden slit while the bearer’s own voice withdraws into silence. After removing the helmet, they must wait until morning before speaking their own name.
use_en: Calls in the stored voice to those its original speaker once named, crossing noise and distance within one battlefield.

form_en: Silver shield with a person-shaped empty centre
lore_en:
When burial crews opened the city gate, they found the shield standing in the empty road. A departing figure moved within its silver centre, though only burnt houses stood behind it. The figure walked through many seasons, awaiting someone to complete the final withdrawal.

Whoever uses the shield to draw someone from danger sees that figure take the rescued person’s shape. Thereafter the path between them becomes an absence around which attacks must pass. Arrows fall to either side, fire parts beneath their steps, and even an entering blade is drawn beyond the silver rim. Protection lasts only while the rescued person advances towards safety. Should they return to die in the bearer’s place, the world closes their reserved space at once, leaving a hollow silver centre amid the battle.
use_en: Reserves a corridor empty of attacks between the bearer and one person being brought to safety.

form_en: Smoke-white cuirass without heraldry
lore_en:
On a field that had changed hands many times, two survivors of a duel placed their hands upon white armour. Their final blows stopped within its rivets, weighing enough to sink the earth beneath it into a ring. They removed the armour, abandoned their weapons and departed in opposite directions at dawn.

Ever since, the armour can receive the ending of a contest both parties sincerely relinquish. Every injury still unformed within their final blows passes into the steel; a broken sword remains within a hand, fire hangs about the shoulders like mourning cloth. Both may leave the place that would have ended them. Yet the armour stays, holding all that destruction until they return together to settle its burden. Whoever betrays the truce calls that ending upon their own body.
use_en: Receives two killing blows when both adversaries freely end their contest.

form_en: White wooden bow carrying one black feather
lore_en:
The bow returned from a city whose roads snow had erased. A letter from a messenger who never reached home still hung upon its string, while the black feather on its limb grew small branches along the vanished streets. No one opened that letter; its first keeper merely tied news of survivors to an arrow.

An arrow follows a road the archer once walked entire, however many snowy lands or seasons of separation now lie along it. People beside the route hear running footsteps without seeing anyone, and the arrow reaches the door still standing at memory’s end. If a stretch has been destroyed, the bow burns its feather-branch to carry the arrow across one final time. Each such journey permanently erases part of the living map upon the bow.
use_en: Sends a message or light line along a route the archer once walked, crossing the distance of that road.

form_en: Silver gauntlet with a clouded mirror palm
lore_en:
A silversmith died in an empty house, leaving gloves and the cup he had given his child. The cup had been recovered from a riverbed three seasons earlier; on the burial night it returned to the half-closed glove, whole as when first given. Two hands opening towards each other remained visible within the silver.

The glove records a freely given object and holds that instant beyond decay. When its bearer calls the image in the palm, the real object returns in the condition in which it was received, drawing its scattered fragments from their resting places. On its journey it is only a silver shadow passing through seams of light; it regains weight upon touching the glove. Its giver must remain alive and acknowledge the gift, for the power rests within a trust still unwithdrawn.
use_en: Calls back a gift, restoring damage incurred after it was entrusted to the glove.

form_en: Small steel hammer with a lightless striking face
lore_en:
At the heart of a ruined fortress, an intact nail passed through stone deeper than the walls’ foundations. Beside it lay a small hammer whose handle bore a word worn by countless hands: choose. Blows radiated around it in rings, while the central nail held a straight course through every stone layer.

The wielder rests the hammer’s face upon one point and chooses the next stroke’s direction. When the hammer lifts, the entire weight pressing upon that point gathers into a single line of force. One stroke may lift a gate bar from a mountain or separate a tower’s foot from its foundations, precise to a nail-head’s width. The wielder’s hand must maintain its chosen direction until the force has passed; the world carries every error through in full.
use_en: Gathers pressure upon one point into a single directed stroke, sufficient to release or break immense structures.

form_en: Silver pistol with a sealed empty chamber
lore_en:
The pistol was found aboard a ship stripped of every mast, in a skeleton’s hand pointing towards shore. Its sealed chamber was empty, yet whenever the night wind returned, a finger-shaped stain appeared upon the silver, as though the dead still awaited a worthy target. When a living hand first lifted it, a sunken ship’s cannon sounded offshore.

The pistol holds the final shot of every weapon silenced in that sea battle. When its bearer chooses an ending, those unfired rounds join in one line of light through sea, fortress or fleet barring the way. For that instant, those nearby hear the entire old battlefield fire together. Afterwards the silver becomes salt and dissolves from the hand, leaving an indelible stain upon the finger that pulled the trigger.
use_en: Releases one line of fire gathering the sea battle’s final unfired shots stored within the pistol.

form_en: A steel artillery shell carrying a Vestigium-bearing adhering incendiary
lore_en:
Marco set an empty shell upon the table at Fes and opened a vial of red powder. The warmth upon his fingertips was a share of Vestigium that could enter something craftsmen could make repeatedly. Through separate trials of casing and incendiary, Bala de Fuego became a round carrying fire that adhered to timber, cloth and siege machinery amid snow.

Its value emerged in the workshop’s rhythm: batch marks, production dates, firing books and lots dismantled for premature burning. Marco kept the powder to the necessary amount, stored rounds separately and demanded to know how his own people could be saved if the magazine burned. Common Vestigium passed through smiths, foremen and carters to become firepower sustained through a battle.
use_en: Spreads an adhering incendiary when the shell breaks, burning combustible targets and obstructing formations through the fire-covered area.

form_en: Bala de Fuego Inextinguible, a two-layer red-black incendiary
lore_en:
Fuego Negro begins with Marco’s fire-shell and passes through Edward’s technical team. An added reaction layer lets burning droplets continue supplying heat for an interval, making water, vapour and snow unable to extinguish them immediately. Upon the sail-covered test frame, red-black fire clings to cloth, timber and rope; water carries the incendiary elsewhere.

Heat-absorbing mineral sand extinguishes much of it. After the trial, Edward and Isabella limit its allocation during the fleet refit, while requiring separate storage and authority to discard a whole case if it heats abnormally. Fuego Negro grants a naval advantage together with the task of protecting the ship carrying it. Its development lies in two cooperating effects, without requiring replacement of the entire Vestigium input.
use_en: Delivers an adhering incendiary that continues supplying its own heat during its active interval, especially dangerous to sails, rigging and wooden hulls.

form_en: Dew gathering inside a circular boundary
lore_en:
After replacing the glass three times, the craftsman kept its old frame: the anomaly occupied an absence.

One pane in an empty nursery stays dry at its rim and wet in the centre, even after replacement. The circle remains fixed to the frame. Vapour within a handspan gathers centrally instead of coating the cold surface.
use_en: Collects a little dew for inspecting condensation clarity.

form_en: An ash ribbon suspended a finger above a table
lore_en:
A furnace-sweeper brushed the ash away and watched it stand again, refusing his labour.

A furnace test room holds cold ash above one flagstone. Cleaning and adding fresh ash reproduce the same ribbon. Only very light ash remains suspended, revealing each vibration of the table.
use_en: Reveals small tabletop vibrations during a short trial.

form_en: A pale light patch upon dark tiles
lore_en:
A pupil hiding a lamp during a game saw the floor keep its bright eye a beat longer.

An old classroom floor retains a light patch briefly after a lamp is covered. New lamps and resurfacing do not move it. Received light fades through a short measurable delay.
use_en: Compares the order of two light shutters in a small model.

form_en: A thin amber haze in a corner
lore_en:
Every morning the keeper visited the empty corner to smell timber carted away long before.

An empty store corner smells of fresh timber after its boards are removed. Another wood sample leaves a scent that fades before morning. The air pocket retains a deposited object’s scent longer than the surrounding room.
use_en: Compares timber scents in separate trials.

form_en: A dew footprint upon a stone step
lore_en:
Dry footprints on washed stone made the watchman turn before the door shut.

A store stair shows moisture after someone crosses its final step. Dry footwear and a cleaned surface leave the same result. The step retains the latest footprint outline for several minutes.
use_en: Indicates a recent passage while an attendant is elsewhere.

form_en: Rhythmic light points in a mortar joint
lore_en:
A craftsman removed the clock for repair and listened as the wall carried on its duty.

A workshop wall keeps ticking after its clock is removed. Fresh pointing retains the rhythm at lower volume. The joint briefly repeats an even beat tapped against the wall.
